body.p: The Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables developers to build secure, two-way connections between their data sources and AI-powered tools.

You can configure a reference to an MCP configuration file, other related options, and view details about the connection status in the
Preferences Plugins / Oxygen AI Positron / Model Context Protocol (MCP) page.

dd.p: Specify the path to a JSON file that defines the MCP servers to load. AI Positron utilizes this file to load extra tools that can be called by the AI engine when using the chat modes or when invoking custom AI actions. The path to the configuration file can be either absolute or it can contain Oxygen editor variables (such as the project directory variable ${pd}).
Because there is no single standard MCP configuration file format used by all clients, AI Positron accepts the following top-level server container names:

ul.li: servers - Also supported for compatibility with other MCP clients.

dd.p: Each server entry can describe one of the following connection types:

ul.li: Local stdio server - Starts a local process and communicates with it through standard input/output streams.
Remote Streamable HTTP server - Connects to a remote MCP endpoint over HTTP.
Remote SSE server (deprecated) - Connects to a remote MCP endpoint that uses Server-Sent Events.

dd.p: If you change the Configuration file, Allow running local MCP servers, or Connection timeout (seconds) options, clicking Apply or OK reloads the MCP servers using the applied option values and the current configuration file content. You can also use the Reload action placed next to the Configuration file option. If you edit the JSON file content afterwards, come back to this preferences page and use Reload.
dd.note: For configuration files that contain API key values, you can use Oxygen editor variables to avoid setting key values directly in the configuration file. You can also use editor variables in the url, command, args, cwd, and headers properties (for example, to access environment variables or system properties).

dlentry.dd: The configured timeout for attempts to connect to each server or retrieve content from it.

Selecting this option allows local MCP servers to run as external processes.Local MCP servers are run as processes from the current user account and have full access to the computer resources as all other processes run in the user account. Before enabling this option, you need to ensure that your configuration starts a secure MCP server and does not expose you to security risks.

dlentry.dt: Add provided tools to all chat modes
dlentry.dd: Enabled by default, this option allows all defined chat modes to access the tools provided by the MCP servers during conversations.

dlentry.dt: Allow running the Oxygen XML application as a local MCP server (Experimental)
dlentry.dd: If enabled, external applications are allowed to programmatically start and control the Oxygen XML application. For more details, see .
For HTTP MCP servers that use OAuth authentication, buttons are available to Sign in to all servers and Sign out from all servers.

dd.p: Shows a summary of the configured MCP servers, including how many servers are configured and how many are currently connected, not connected, or skipped (for example, if local servers are defined in the configuration file, but running them is disallowed by the preferences).

Below the summary, the connection details are grouped in the following tabs:
Servers - Lists each configured server and its current connection state. For servers that are skipped or not connected, a tooltip shows the reason. The last column shows Sign in/Sign out buttons for the servers that use OAuth authentication.
Logging - Shows the connection log for the configured MCP servers.
dd.note: All the tools loaded from an MCP server have their names prefixed with the name of the MCP server. This allows multiple servers to provide tools with the same name. For example, if a tool name is search and is loaded from an MCP server named mcp-web-access, the tool name that needs to be referenced in a custom AI action is mcp-web-access_search.

For HTTP MCP servers that use OAuth, the optional oauth object can include properties such as authorize_url, token_url, client_id, client_secret, scopes, redirect_uri, additional_authorize_params, and resource.

For remote HTTP-based connections, the following properties are supported:

ul.li: url - The remote MCP endpoint URL.
headers - Optional HTTP headers sent when connecting to the server.
type - Optional transport hint. Use sse when the URL does not clearly identify an SSE endpoint.

The following properties are supported for local MCP server connections:

ul.li: command - The executable command used to start the MCP server process (for example, npx, docker, node, python).
args - An array of string arguments to pass to the command.
env - An object that contains environment variables to set for the server process.
cwd - The working directory where the server process is launched.

section.title: Tool Call Security
section.p: AI Positron does not control how various tools are implemented by the configured MCP servers or what parameters are used by the LLM to call them. By default, whenever the LLM calls tools obtained by AI Positron from an MCP server, the end user is required to approve or reject each individual tool call in the Chat view.

section.title: Oxygen XML as a Local MCP Server (Experimental)
section.p: When using 28 or later, the entire Oxygen XML application can be configured and started from a third-party AI assistant (e.g. Claude Desktop or Claude Code) as a local MCP server, providing access to tools for calling specific AI actions, validating, editing, and refactoring XML documents.
